# CBACT04C — Program Specification

## Overview

CBACT04C is the CardDemo monthly interest calculator. It reads the transaction-category balance file (`TCATBALF`) in key sequence — the key is account ID + transaction type code + transaction category code — and, for every category balance belonging to an account, looks up the interest rate that applies to that account's disclosure group and that type/category combination. For each balance with a non-zero rate it computes one month's interest, accumulates it into a per-account running total, and writes an interest transaction record to the output transaction file (`TRANSACT`) attributed to the account's card number. When the driver detects that the account ID has changed from one input record to the next, it posts the accumulated interest for the *previous* account back onto the account master record (`ACCTFILE`), adding it to the current balance and zeroing that account's current-cycle credit and debit totals. Any file status other than the expected values causes the program to display the status and abend.

## Paragraph flow

The `PROCEDURE DIVISION` receives `EXTERNAL-PARMS` (`PARM-LENGTH`, `PARM-DATE`) from the caller and drives everything from a main routine that is not itself a named paragraph. That driver displays `'START OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT04C'`, opens all five files (`0000-`, `0100-`, `0200-`, `0300-`, `0400-`), then runs `PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE = 'Y'`. Inside the loop, when `END-OF-FILE = 'N'` it performs `1000-TCATBALF-GET-NEXT`; if the read did not hit end of file it adds 1 to `WS-RECORD-COUNT`, displays the whole `TRAN-CAT-BAL-RECORD`, and then applies the account-break logic: if `TRANCAT-ACCT-ID NOT= WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM`, it performs `1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT` for the account just finished (unless `WS-FIRST-TIME = 'Y'`, in which case it only flips `WS-FIRST-TIME` to `'N'`), resets `WS-TOTAL-INT` to 0, saves the new account ID into `WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM` and into `FD-ACCT-ID`, performs `1100-GET-ACCT-DATA`, then moves the account ID into `FD-XREF-ACCT-ID` and performs `1110-GET-XREF-DATA`. For every record — break or not — it then builds the disclosure-group key by moving `ACCT-GROUP-ID` to `FD-DIS-ACCT-GROUP-ID`, `TRANCAT-CD` to `FD-DIS-TRAN-CAT-CD` and `TRANCAT-TYPE-CD` to `FD-DIS-TRAN-TYPE-CD`, performs `1200-GET-INTEREST-RATE`, and if `DIS-INT-RATE NOT = 0` performs `1300-COMPUTE-INTEREST` followed by `1400-COMPUTE-FEES`. The `ELSE` branch of the outer `IF END-OF-FILE = 'N'` performs `1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT`, but that branch can never be reached: the `PERFORM UNTIL` condition is tested before each iteration, so once `END-OF-FILE` becomes `'Y'` the loop exits rather than re-entering with the `ELSE` taken. After the loop the driver closes all five files (`9000-` through `9400-`), displays `'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT04C'`, and does `GOBACK`.

Four commented-out `DISPLAY` lines for `ACCT-GROUP-ID`, `TRANCAT-CD` and `TRANCAT-TYPE-CD` sit inside the loop; they are inert and need no Java equivalent.

### 0000-TCATBALF-OPEN

Moves 8 to `APPL-RESULT`, opens `TCATBAL-FILE` for input. If `TCATBALF-STATUS = '00'` it sets `APPL-RESULT` to 0, otherwise 12. If the `APPL-AOK` condition (`APPL-RESULT = 0`) holds it continues; otherwise it displays `'ERROR OPENING TRANSACTION CATEGORY BALANCE'`, copies the file status into `IO-STATUS`, and performs `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` then `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`. Calls: `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS`, `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### 0100-XREFFILE-OPEN

Identical pattern for `XREF-FILE`, opened `INPUT`. On failure it displays `'ERROR OPENING CROSS REF FILE'` together with `XREFFILE-STATUS`, then performs `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` and `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### 0200-DISCGRP-OPEN

Identical pattern for `DISCGRP-FILE`, opened `INPUT`. On failure it displays `'ERROR OPENING DALY REJECTS FILE'` (the message text is a leftover from another program — it refers to the disclosure group file here), then performs `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` and `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### 0300-ACCTFILE-OPEN

Same pattern for `ACCOUNT-FILE`, but opened `I-O` because the program rewrites account records later. On failure it displays `'ERROR OPENING ACCOUNT MASTER FILE'`, then performs `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` and `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### 0400-TRANFILE-OPEN

Same pattern for `TRANSACT-FILE`, opened `OUTPUT` — the transaction file is created fresh each run, so any prior content is discarded. On failure it displays `'ERROR OPENING TRANSACTION FILE'`, then performs `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` and `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### 1000-TCATBALF-GET-NEXT

Reads the next record sequentially: `READ TCATBAL-FILE INTO TRAN-CAT-BAL-RECORD`. Status `'00'` sets `APPL-RESULT` to 0; status `'10'` (end of file) sets it to 16; anything else sets 12. If `APPL-AOK` it continues. Otherwise, if `APPL-EOF` (`APPL-RESULT = 16`) it moves `'Y'` to `END-OF-FILE`; if not, it displays `'ERROR READING TRANSACTION CATEGORY FILE'`, moves the status into `IO-STATUS`, and performs `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` then `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`. Calls: `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS`, `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT

Posts the accumulated interest for the account currently held in `ACCOUNT-RECORD`. It performs `ADD WS-TOTAL-INT TO ACCT-CURR-BAL`, then moves 0 to `ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT` and 0 to `ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT` — the cycle-to-date credit and debit accumulators are reset as part of the same posting. It then does `REWRITE FD-ACCTFILE-REC FROM ACCOUNT-RECORD`. Status `'00'` sets `APPL-RESULT` to 0, otherwise 12; on a non-zero result it displays `'ERROR RE-WRITING ACCOUNT FILE'`, moves `ACCTFILE-STATUS` into `IO-STATUS`, and performs `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` then `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`. Calls: `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS`, `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### 1100-GET-ACCT-DATA

Random-reads the account master by the key already moved into `FD-ACCT-ID`: `READ ACCOUNT-FILE INTO ACCOUNT-RECORD`, with an `INVALID KEY` clause that displays `'ACCOUNT NOT FOUND: '` followed by `FD-ACCT-ID`. Note that the `INVALID KEY` display does not stop processing on its own — control falls through to the status check, where anything other than `'00'` sets `APPL-RESULT` to 12 and leads to `'ERROR READING ACCOUNT FILE'`, `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS`, and `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`. So a missing account is displayed and then abends. Calls: `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS`, `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### 1110-GET-XREF-DATA

Random-reads the card cross-reference file through its alternate key: `READ XREF-FILE INTO CARD-XREF-RECORD KEY IS FD-XREF-ACCT-ID`, with an `INVALID KEY` clause displaying `'ACCOUNT NOT FOUND: '` and `FD-XREF-ACCT-ID`. As above, the status check follows: `'00'` gives `APPL-RESULT` 0, anything else 12, which leads to `'ERROR READING XREF FILE'`, `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS`, and `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`. The purpose is to obtain `XREF-CARD-NUM`, which is stamped onto the interest transaction. Calls: `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS`, `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### 1200-GET-INTEREST-RATE

Random-reads the disclosure group file on the key built from `ACCT-GROUP-ID` + `TRANCAT-TYPE-CD` + `TRANCAT-CD`: `READ DISCGRP-FILE INTO DIS-GROUP-RECORD`, with an `INVALID KEY` clause that displays `'DISCLOSURE GROUP RECORD MISSING'` and `'TRY WITH DEFAULT GROUP CODE'`. The status check here is deliberately more permissive: `DISCGRP-STATUS = '00' OR '23'` sets `APPL-RESULT` to 0 — a "record not found" (`'23'`) is a tolerated outcome, not an error. Anything else sets 12 and leads to `'ERROR READING DISCLOSURE GROUP FILE'`, `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS`, and `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`. Finally, if `DISCGRP-STATUS = '23'`, it moves the literal `'DEFAULT'` into `FD-DIS-ACCT-GROUP-ID` (leaving the type and category parts of the key as they were) and performs `1200-A-GET-DEFAULT-INT-RATE`. Calls: `1200-A-GET-DEFAULT-INT-RATE`, `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS`, `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### 1200-A-GET-DEFAULT-INT-RATE

Re-reads `DISCGRP-FILE INTO DIS-GROUP-RECORD` using the key whose group ID is now `'DEFAULT'`. Here there is no tolerance for `'23'`: only `'00'` sets `APPL-RESULT` to 0; anything else sets 12 and produces `'ERROR READING DEFAULT DISCLOSURE GROUP'`, `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS`, and `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`. A missing default rate row for a given type/category is therefore fatal. Calls: `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS`, `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### 1300-COMPUTE-INTEREST

The core calculation:

```
COMPUTE WS-MONTHLY-INT
 = ( TRAN-CAT-BAL * DIS-INT-RATE) / 1200
```

In plain English: multiply the category balance by the annual interest rate (expressed as a percentage), then divide by 1200 — that is, divide by 100 to turn the percentage into a fraction and by 12 to turn the annual rate into one month's worth. The result lands in `WS-MONTHLY-INT`, which is `S9(09)V99` (`BigDecimal`, precision 11, scale 2). There is no `ROUNDED` phrase, so the result is truncated to two decimal places, not rounded.

It then does `ADD WS-MONTHLY-INT TO WS-TOTAL-INT`, accumulating this category's interest into the per-account total that `1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT` will later post, and performs `1300-B-WRITE-TX`. Calls: `1300-B-WRITE-TX`.

### 1300-B-WRITE-TX

Builds and writes one interest transaction record. It adds 1 to `WS-TRANID-SUFFIX`, then constructs the transaction ID:

```
STRING PARM-DATE,
       WS-TRANID-SUFFIX
  DELIMITED BY SIZE
  INTO TRAN-ID
```

`PARM-DATE` is `X(10)` and `WS-TRANID-SUFFIX` is `9(06)`, so the concatenation exactly fills the `X(16)` `TRAN-ID` — the run date followed by a zero-padded six-digit sequence number that is monotonically increasing across the whole run (it is never reset per account).

It then populates the rest of `TRAN-RECORD`: `'01'` to `TRAN-TYPE-CD`, `'05'` to `TRAN-CAT-CD`, `'System'` to `TRAN-SOURCE`; a description built as

```
STRING 'Int. for a/c ' ,
       ACCT-ID
       DELIMITED BY SIZE
 INTO TRAN-DESC
```

(the literal `'Int. for a/c '` followed by the 11-digit account ID, left-justified in the `X(100)` field); `WS-MONTHLY-INT` to `TRAN-AMT`; 0 to `TRAN-MERCHANT-ID`; spaces to `TRAN-MERCHANT-NAME`, `TRAN-MERCHANT-CITY` and `TRAN-MERCHANT-ZIP`; and `XREF-CARD-NUM` (from the cross-reference read) to `TRAN-CARD-NUM`. It performs `Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP` and moves the resulting `DB2-FORMAT-TS` into both `TRAN-ORIG-TS` and `TRAN-PROC-TS` — the two timestamps are always identical for these generated records.

Finally `WRITE FD-TRANFILE-REC FROM TRAN-RECORD`; status `'00'` sets `APPL-RESULT` to 0, otherwise 12, leading to `'ERROR WRITING TRANSACTION RECORD'`, `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS`, and `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`. Note that `TRAN-CAT-CD` is a numeric `9(04)` field receiving the two-character literal `'05'`; a Java implementation should reproduce the resulting stored value (5) rather than the literal characters. Calls: `Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP`, `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS`, `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### 1400-COMPUTE-FEES

Empty. The body is a comment reading `* To be implemented` followed by `EXIT.` It is performed once per category balance whose rate is non-zero, but does nothing. A Java implementation should keep the call site as a no-op extension point.

### 9000-TCATBALF-CLOSE

Moves 8 to `APPL-RESULT`, closes `TCATBAL-FILE`, checks for `'00'` (0) versus anything else (12), and on failure displays `'ERROR CLOSING TRANSACTION BALANCE FILE'` then performs `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` and `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### 9100-XREFFILE-CLOSE

Same close-and-check pattern for `XREF-FILE`; failure message `'ERROR CLOSING CROSS REF FILE'`, then `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` and `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### 9200-DISCGRP-CLOSE

Same pattern for `DISCGRP-FILE`; failure message `'ERROR CLOSING DISCLOSURE GROUP FILE'`, then `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` and `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### 9300-ACCTFILE-CLOSE

Same pattern for `ACCOUNT-FILE`; failure message `'ERROR CLOSING ACCOUNT FILE'`, then `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` and `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### 9400-TRANFILE-CLOSE

Same pattern for `TRANSACT-FILE`; failure message `'ERROR CLOSING TRANSACTION FILE'`, then `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` and `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP

Formats the current system time as a 26-character DB2-style timestamp. It moves `FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE` into `COBOL-TS` (whose subfields are `COB-YYYY`, `COB-MM`, `COB-DD`, `COB-HH`, `COB-MIN`, `COB-SS`, `COB-MIL`, `COB-REST`), then copies each component into the corresponding subfield of the redefinition of `DB2-FORMAT-TS`, moves `'0000'` into `DB2-REST`, `'-'` into `DB2-STREEP-1`, `DB2-STREEP-2` and `DB2-STREEP-3`, and `'.'` into `DB2-DOT-1`, `DB2-DOT-2` and `DB2-DOT-3`. The layout is documented in a comment as `EEEE-MM-DD-UU.MM.SS.HH0000` — i.e. `yyyy-MM-dd-HH.mm.ss.` followed by hundredths of a second and four zero digits, filling all 26 characters. A commented-out `DISPLAY 'DB2-TIMESTAMP = ' DB2-FORMAT-TS` is inert. Note that the subfields this paragraph writes into are all `REDEFINES` fields and are therefore flagged for human review below; the target `DB2-FORMAT-TS` itself is `X(26)`.

### 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM

Displays `'ABENDING PROGRAM'`, moves 0 to `TIMING` and 999 to `ABCODE`, then issues `CALL 'CEE3ABD' USING ABCODE, TIMING` — the Language Environment abend service, which terminates the job with user abend code 999 and does not return. In Java this is a hard, non-recoverable failure exit.

### 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS

Renders a file status into a four-character display string. If `IO-STATUS` is not numeric, or `IO-STAT1 = '9'`, it moves `IO-STAT1` into the first byte of `IO-STATUS-04` via reference modification `IO-STATUS-04(1:1)`, zeroes `TWO-BYTES-BINARY`, moves `IO-STAT2` into `TWO-BYTES-RIGHT` (the low-order byte of that binary field, via its `REDEFINES`), moves `TWO-BYTES-BINARY` into `IO-STATUS-0403`, and displays `'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN'` followed by `IO-STATUS-04` — this converts the binary second status byte into its decimal value, which is how VSAM extended statuses like `9xx` are reported. Otherwise it moves `'0000'` into `IO-STATUS-04`, overlays the two status characters at `IO-STATUS-04(3:2)`, and displays the same message. The `TWO-BYTES-LEFT` / `TWO-BYTES-RIGHT` fields it depends on are flagged for human review below.

## Business rules

- **Driving sequence.** Input is read sequentially from the indexed transaction-category-balance file in key order (account ID, transaction type code, transaction category code). Records for one account are therefore contiguous, and this is what makes the single-key account-break logic correct.
- **Account break.** When `TRANCAT-ACCT-ID` differs from `WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM`, the previous account is posted via `1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT`, then `WS-TOTAL-INT` is reset to 0 and the new account's master record and cross-reference record are read. On the very first record only (`WS-FIRST-TIME = 'Y'`), the posting step is skipped and `WS-FIRST-TIME` is set to `'N'`.
- **Comparison caveat.** `WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM` is `X(11)` (String) while `TRANCAT-ACCT-ID` is `9(11)` (BigDecimal, precision 11, scale 0). The comparison and the `MOVE` between them are a numeric-to-alphanumeric transfer of the 11 digit characters; a Java implementation must compare the 11-character zero-padded digit strings, and must treat the initial value of `WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM` as spaces (which never equals a digit string, so the first record always takes the break path).
- **Interest formula, exactly.** `COMPUTE WS-MONTHLY-INT = ( TRAN-CAT-BAL * DIS-INT-RATE) / 1200`. No `ROUNDED` phrase is present, so the result is **truncated** toward zero to two decimal places when stored into `WS-MONTHLY-INT` (`S9(09)V99`). Java must use `RoundingMode.DOWN` at scale 2 on the final store, not `HALF_UP`.
- **Zero-rate skip.** Interest is computed and a transaction written only when `DIS-INT-RATE NOT = 0`. A zero rate produces no transaction record and contributes nothing to `WS-TOTAL-INT`. `1400-COMPUTE-FEES` is likewise only reached for non-zero rates.
- **Default rate fallback.** If the disclosure-group lookup returns status `'23'` (not found), the group ID portion of the key is replaced with the literal `'DEFAULT'` (transaction type and category unchanged) and the read is retried. A failure on that retry is fatal. On the `'23'` path, `DIS-GROUP-RECORD` retains its previous contents until the retry succeeds — the retry is what supplies the rate actually used.
- **Posting to the account.** `1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT` adds `WS-TOTAL-INT` to `ACCT-CURR-BAL` and unconditionally zeroes `ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT` and `ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT`, then rewrites the record. The cycle-total reset happens even if `WS-TOTAL-INT` is zero.
- **End-of-file handling — the last account is not posted.** The `PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE = 'Y'` loop tests its condition before each iteration, so once `1000-TCATBALF-GET-NEXT` sets `END-OF-FILE` to `'Y'` the loop exits immediately. The `ELSE PERFORM 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT` branch intended to flush the final account is unreachable, and the last account group's accumulated `WS-TOTAL-INT` is never written to the account master (its interest transactions *are* written to the transaction file). A faithful Java port must reproduce this behavior; changing it is a business decision for a human, not a translation detail.
- **Transaction record content.** Every generated transaction has `TRAN-TYPE-CD = '01'`, `TRAN-CAT-CD = '05'`, `TRAN-SOURCE = 'System'`, merchant ID 0, blank merchant name/city/zip, description `'Int. for a/c '` + account ID, amount = that category's `WS-MONTHLY-INT`, card number from the cross-reference record, and identical origination and processing timestamps.
- **Transaction ID uniqueness.** `TRAN-ID` = `PARM-DATE` (10 chars) + `WS-TRANID-SUFFIX` (6 digits, incremented once per written transaction, never reset). Uniqueness within a run depends on the counter; uniqueness across runs depends on the caller passing a distinct `PARM-DATE`. The counter wraps at 999999.
- **Output file is replaced.** `TRANSACT-FILE` is opened `OUTPUT`, so each run starts an empty transaction file.
- **Error posture.** Every I/O operation checks its file status. The only tolerated non-`'00'` statuses are `'10'` on the sequential read (end of file) and `'23'` on the first disclosure-group read (triggers the `'DEFAULT'` fallback). Every other non-`'00'` status displays a message, displays the formatted status, and abends via `CEE3ABD` with abend code 999. `INVALID KEY` on the account and cross-reference reads displays `'ACCOUNT NOT FOUND: '` and then still falls through to the status check, which abends.
- **Timestamp format.** `TRAN-ORIG-TS` and `TRAN-PROC-TS` are a 26-character string of the form `yyyy-MM-dd-HH.mm.ss.` + two-digit hundredths + `0000`, taken from `FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE` at the moment each transaction is built.

## Flagged for human review

These fields were deliberately not mapped by this repo's parser. Per ADR-0002 (`docs/adr/0002-a-hand-rolled-parser-for-a-deliberately-bounded-grammar.md`), `REDEFINES` is outside the bounded grammar and must be resolved by a human rather than guessed. No Java shape is proposed for any of them.

- **`TWO-BYTES-LEFT`** — declared under `01 TWO-BYTES-ALPHA REDEFINES TWO-BYTES-BINARY`; it is a byte-level alias over a binary field, so its Java representation depends on a human decision about mainframe byte layout, not on a `PIC` clause.
- **`TWO-BYTES-RIGHT`** — same `REDEFINES` group; it is the low-order byte of `TWO-BYTES-BINARY` and is actively written by `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` to decode an extended file status, so the byte-order semantics must be confirmed by a human before porting.
- **`DB2-YYYY`** — part of `01 FILLER REDEFINES DB2-FORMAT-TS`; an overlay of the 26-character timestamp string, written by `Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP`.
- **`DB2-MIN`** — same timestamp `REDEFINES` overlay; minutes component.
- **`DB2-DOT-2`** — same timestamp `REDEFINES` overlay; a literal `.` separator character.
- **`DB2-SS`** — same timestamp `REDEFINES` overlay; seconds component.
- **`DB2-DOT-3`** — same timestamp `REDEFINES` overlay; a literal `.` separator character.
- **`DB2-MIL`** — same timestamp `REDEFINES` overlay; hundredths-of-a-second component, and the only numeric (`PIC 9(002)`) subfield in the overlay.
- **`DB2-REST`** — same timestamp `REDEFINES` overlay; the trailing four characters, always set to `'0000'`.

Practical note for the human gate: the whole `DB2-*` group exists only to assemble `DB2-FORMAT-TS` (`X(26)`, mapped) inside `Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP`. A Java port will most likely replace the overlay with direct string formatting of the timestamp rather than modelling each subfield — but that substitution is a human call, and the same applies to `TWO-BYTES-LEFT`/`TWO-BYTES-RIGHT` in `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS`.

steps.description: Opens the transaction-category-balance, cross-reference and disclosure-group inputs, the account master for update and the transaction output (replaced each run), abending on any status other than '00'.
Reads the next transaction-category-balance record sequentially in key order (account ID, type code, category code), treating status '10' as end of file.

On an account break, randomly reads the account master by account ID and the card cross-reference by its alternate account key, attaching both to the category balance so the card number is available for the interest transaction.
Reads the disclosure group on the account group ID plus transaction type and category, tolerating status '23' by retrying the read with the group ID replaced by the literal 'DEFAULT'.

Computes (TRAN-CAT-BAL * DIS-INT-RATE) / 1200 truncated to scale 2 into WS-MONTHLY-INT for this category balance, which is also summed per account into the group accumulator posted by postAccountInterest.
No-op extension point performed once per non-zero-rate category balance; passes the accrued item through unchanged.

Builds one interest transaction from the accrued item — ID of PARM-DATE plus a run-wide six-digit suffix, type '01', category 5, source 'System', amount WS-MONTHLY-INT, card number from the cross-reference and identical origination/processing timestamps — and writes it to the transaction file.
For each completed account group, adds the accumulated WS-TOTAL-INT to ACCT-CURR-BAL, zeroes ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT and ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT, and rewrites the account master record.
steps.guard_condition: TRANCAT-ACCT-ID NOT= WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM AND WS-FIRST-TIME NOT = 'Y'

steps.description: Closes all five files at end of run, abending on any close status other than '00'.
